question: How does a commercial property policy value a loss, and what is coinsurance actually doing to my payment?
aliases: actual cash value versus replacement cost commercial property
agreed value optional coverage suspends coinsurance
must I actually rebuild to get replacement cost
shortAnswer: The default is actual cash value, and everything better than that is an exception you have to have bought. The Valuation condition states that the insurer will determine the value of Covered Property at actual cash value as of the time of loss, except as provided in the subparagraphs that follow [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Replacement Cost is an Optional Coverage that applies only if shown in the Declarations, and it replaces Actual Cash Value in that condition [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Coinsurance is a separate Additional Condition that applies only if a coinsurance percentage is shown [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12], and where it bites it reduces the payment before the deductible is subtracted [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
assumes: The policy uses the Building And Personal Property Coverage Form in the 10 12 edition [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12], with the policy issued governing over anything described here.
A Limit of Insurance is shown for the type of property in question, since Covered Property means the described types only if a limit is shown for that type [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
You are asking how the loss is measured, not whether the cause of loss is covered, which the Causes of Loss form answers.
why:
Four mechanisms decide the number, and they run in a particular order.

First, what is covered property at all. Covered Property means the types described in section A.1 and limited by Property Not Covered, if a Limit Of Insurance is shown in the Declarations for that type [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Your Business Personal Property is property in or on the described building or in the open, or in a vehicle, within 100 feet of the building or within 100 feet of the described premises, whichever distance is greater; Personal Property Of Others is property in the insured's care, custody or control within the same footprint [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Property beyond that radius is a different conversation. Coverage Extensions apply within that footprint too, and are available only where a coinsurance percentage of 80 percent or more, or a Value Reporting period symbol, is shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Second, valuation. The default is actual cash value at the time of loss, subject to four exceptions [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Small building losses are one: where the Building limit satisfies the Coinsurance condition and the cost to repair or replace is $2,500 or less, the form pays the cost of repairs or replacement, expressly excluding any increased cost attributable to an ordinance or law, and expressly valuing awnings, floor coverings, appliances for refrigerating, ventilating, cooking, dishwashing or laundering, and outdoor equipment or furniture at actual cash value even when attached to the building [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Stock sold but not delivered is valued at the selling price less discounts and expenses otherwise incurred; glass at the cost of replacement with safety glazing where law requires it; and tenants' improvements and betterments in three branches, at actual cash value if the insured repairs promptly, at a proportion of original cost computed from the days remaining on the lease over the days from installation to lease expiration if it does not, and at nothing if others pay for the repairs [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. A tenant who delays repairs is paid on a fraction that shrinks as the lease runs down.

Third, coinsurance, which is a condition on adequacy rather than a limit. It applies only if a percentage is shown [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12], and where one limit applies to two or more separate items it is applied to the total of all property that limit covers [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The insurer will not pay the full amount of a loss if the value of Covered Property at the time of loss multiplied by the coinsurance percentage is greater than the Limit of Insurance [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The calculation multiplies value at the time of loss by the percentage, divides the Limit of Insurance by that figure, multiplies the total loss before any deductible by the result, then subtracts the deductible, and pays that or the Limit of Insurance, whichever is less [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The form then says plainly what happens to the rest: for the remainder the insured will either have to rely on other insurance or absorb the loss itself [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Note the order, because it costs money. The Deductible section provides that the insurer first reduces the amount of loss if required by the Coinsurance condition or the Agreed Value Optional Coverage, pays nothing if the adjusted loss is at or below the deductible, and otherwise subtracts the deductible from the adjusted loss [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. The coinsurance reduction happens first and the deductible comes off what is left. One further mechanic is worth knowing: where an occurrence damages more than one item of Covered Property with separate limits, the losses are not combined in determining application of the deductible, but the deductible applies only once per occurrence [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Fourth, the Optional Coverages, which apply only if shown as applicable in the Declarations: Agreed Value, Inflation Guard, Replacement Cost, and Extension Of Replacement Cost To Personal Property Of Others [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

Agreed Value switches coinsurance off for the property it applies to, and pays no more than the proportion that the Limit of Insurance bears to the Agreed Value shown in the Declarations [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. It has an expiry, and the expiry has teeth: if the Agreed Value expiration date shown is not extended, the Coinsurance condition is reinstated and the Optional Coverage expires [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Its terms apply only to loss occurring on or after its effective date and before the earlier of that expiration date or the policy expiration date [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. A lapsed agreed value schedule quietly puts coinsurance back.

Inflation Guard increases the limit automatically by the annual percentage shown, computed as the limit that applied at the most recent inception, anniversary or amending change, times the annual percentage, times the days elapsed divided by 365 [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. It accrues daily rather than stepping at renewal.

Replacement Cost substitutes replacement cost without deduction for depreciation for actual cash value in the Valuation condition [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12], but it does not apply to personal property of others, contents of a residence, works of art, antiques or rare articles including etchings, pictures, statuary, marbles, bronzes, porcelains and bric-a-brac, or Stock unless the Including Stock option is shown [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. And it is conditional on doing the work: the insurer will not pay on a replacement cost basis until the property is actually repaired or replaced, and unless that is done as soon as reasonably possible [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. There is a practical route through that, and it has a deadline: the insured may make a claim on an actual cash value basis and still claim the additional replacement cost amount if it notifies the insurer of its intent within 180 days after the loss [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Tenants' improvements get their own treatment under it, valued as the proportion-of-original-cost branch where the repair conditions are not met, and nothing where others pay; and the Optional Coverage states that improvements and betterments are not considered personal property of others under its terms [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

The fourth option exists because of the third's first carve-out. Extension Of Replacement Cost To Personal Property Of Others may be shown only if Replacement Cost is itself shown, deletes the personal-property-of-others exclusion from it, and provides that where a written contract governs the insured's liability for an item, valuation is based on the amount the insured is liable for under that contract, capped at the lesser of replacement cost or the applicable Limit of Insurance [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].

One further condition worth naming: the Mortgageholders condition pays covered loss to buildings to each mortgageholder shown in the Declarations in their order of precedence, as interests may appear [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
whatChanges: Whether a Limit of Insurance is shown for the type of property, since without one it is not Covered Property [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether the property was within 100 feet of the building or the described premises, whichever is greater [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether a coinsurance percentage is shown, and whether the limit meets the value at the time of loss times that percentage [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether Replacement Cost is shown as applicable, and whether the property is one of the four categories it does not reach [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether the property has actually been repaired or replaced, and whether that was done as soon as reasonably possible [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether 180 days have passed since the loss, which is the window to claim actual cash value first and replacement cost after [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Whether an Agreed Value expiration date has passed without extension, which reinstates coinsurance [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
For a tenant, whether improvements were repaired promptly and how much of the lease remains, since both change the valuation branch [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
variability: This describes the 10 12 edition of the form [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12]. Endorsements change valuation, deductibles and optional coverages, and the policy issued governs.

Coinsurance measures the limit against the value of Covered Property at the time of loss [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12], so adequacy is only known after the loss and depends on a valuation that is itself often contested.
Actual cash value is not defined in the material recorded here, and how depreciation is measured is not settled by this record.
Whether repairs were made as soon as reasonably possible is a factual judgement the form frames and does not resolve [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
nextActions: Check the Declarations for whether Replacement Cost is shown as applicable, rather than assuming a commercial policy carries it [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Check whether a coinsurance percentage is shown, since the condition applies only if one is [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Value the property as it would be valued at the time of loss, not at the time the limit was set, because that is the figure the condition tests against [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
If a loss has occurred and rebuilding may be slow, give notice of intent to claim replacement cost within 180 days and take actual cash value in the meantime [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
Diary any Agreed Value expiration date, because letting it pass reinstates coinsurance [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
If you are a tenant with improvements, repair promptly or understand that valuation moves to a fraction of original cost that shrinks with the lease [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
If you hold others' property, ask whether the Extension Of Replacement Cost To Personal Property Of Others is shown, since Replacement Cost alone excludes it [S:iso-cp-00-10-10-12].
author: Aaron Bollinger

handoff.reason: Coinsurance tests the limit against the value of property at the time of loss, so whether a limit is adequate is a valuation exercise on a particular building and its contents. That is broker and appraiser work rather than something readable off the form.
